A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASCOOD study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original ASCOOD detection results, classification accuracies, ablations, and sensitivity analyses across six ID datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds ImageNet-100 experiments, i-ODIN evaluations, and expanded loss and normalization ablations.

M1.justification: The ASCOOD synthesis and training procedure remains essentially unchanged, but v3 adds a separate inference procedure, i-ODIN. Appendix B modifies ODIN through gradient-based masking of input perturbations; Section 5 and Appendix G.1 describe selective color-channel perturbation. Pixel shuffling itself already appeared in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet-100 classification and OOD evaluation, including SSB-Hard, beyond the six retained ASCOOD benchmarks. Its separate i-ODIN evaluation also introduces ImageNet-200 and ImageNet-1k near/far-OOD coverage and CIFAR-100 near-OOD testing (Appendix G.1).

E2.justification: NPOS changes from a cited method to an evaluated comparator across retained benchmarks. v3 also adds Dream-OOD comparisons on ImageNet-100 and i-ODIN comparisons. Rows labelled KNN disappear from the five appendix comparisons in v2 Tables 21–23, 26, and 30; these are not merely renamed rows.

E3.justification: New ImageNet-100 experiments use a pretrained ResNet-34, 20 fine-tuning epochs, batch size 40, and learning rate 0.0005, with EBO scoring for the reported ASCOOD variants. v3 also adds a separate exact-OpenOOD near/far evaluation for i-ODIN and crossed loss/normalization controls. Original benchmark splits and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Table 5 compares raw and standardized features; v3 Table 8 crosses raw, L2-normalized, and standardized features with KL and energy losses. Tables 30–31 additionally compare the losses on ImageNet-100. Existing sensitivity studies mostly move unchanged, while the Waterbirds ID-as-outlier and gradient-subtraction controls from v2 Table 4 disappear.

E5.justification: Both versions use point estimates and unexplained ± entries without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Retained uncertainty reporting is unchanged; the additional results do not establish a new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive ImageNet, i-ODIN, baseline, and ablation results while retaining the original headline ASCOOD scores. New ImageNet-100 averages are 23.12/94.02 FPR@95/AUROC for KL-ASCOOD versus 16.84/95.93 for NPOS. Matched Aircraft entries also change: shuffle FPR@95 from 47.86 to 47.98 and raw-feature FPR@95 from 59.54 to 55.21. Removed comparator and control rows remove results.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds mathematical definitions of i-ODIN's gradient mask and selectively perturbed input (Equations 8–9). The original OOD definitions, Propositions 1–2, and their proofs remain unchanged; no additional theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim of unified, ID-only ASCOOD detection is retained. The introduction adds an improved ODIN variant to the contributions and explicitly promotes ID pixel shuffling as a strong synthesis baseline; Section 3.1 strengthens the novelty framing of the already-existing shuffle procedure.

C2.justification: v3 adds a qualitative argument that on-the-fly ASCOOD synthesis avoids diffusion models' computational and domain-knowledge dependencies. It also interprets the new loss comparison and explains weak sensitivity to pixel-mask size through larger gradients in invariant regions. The gradient-addition versus subtraction explanation largely moves from v2's appendix.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Table 9 add ImageNet-100 training and synthesis parameters. Existing implementation details are consolidated, and the code-access information is unchanged. The earlier disclosure that the Waterbirds sigma sensitivity study uses pinv=15% is dropped without establishing an actual experimental change.

R1.justification: Positioning expands substantially to diffusion and foundation-model approaches, outlier diversity, and the relationship to VoSo. Added works include Dream-OOD, DiffGuard, CLIPN, and DOS, with substantive comparisons in Sections 1, 5, and 6. The ARPL discussion and citation are removed.

P1.justification: Experimental exposition is substantially reorganized: training details and Section 5.2 move into Appendix D, the gradient-addition explanation moves into Section 5.1, and normalization discussions are consolidated. Supplementary experiments are reordered around the new i-ODIN appendix. The core ASCOOD method exposition remains largely stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds dataset, ImageNet, and i-ODIN tables and expands the normalization table into a loss-by-feature comparison. Sensitivity tables are regrouped into Table 16, and the Waterbirds UMAP figure moves from the main text to Appendix D. Existing image examples and confidence plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded loss-by-normalization ablation better separates design choices than v2 Table 5, and ImageNet-100 comparisons provide useful evidence about broader applicability. Gains are tempered by reporting problems: main Table 3 omits NPOS, which outperforms ASCOOD in appendix Table 30, and the highlighted SSB-Hard AUROC of 83.91 belongs to the energy-loss variant rather than default KL-ASCOOD (Table 31). The added evidence supports a modest net improvement, with qualification of the new summaries still needed.
